hypothesis_text: Aggressive market order execution that moves the final transaction price away from the order book midpoint (|midprice_book| > 1.0 bp) indicates persistent directional order flow rather than transient quote noise in high-beta altcoins. Over a 1h to 4h horizon, this orderbook dislocation predicts short-term continuation in the direction of the trade pressure, with the strongest persistence occurring when orderbook depth imbalance confirms the move and spreads remain tight.
narrative: In cryptocurrency perpetual futures markets, the relationship between trade prices and the prevailing limit order book midpoint is an instantaneous indicator of liquidity consumption. When trades execute persistently at the best bid or best ask, moving the transaction price away from the midpoint by more than 1 basis point at bar close, it reflects aggressive market participant demand exceeding immediate resting liquidity. Unlike slower momentum metrics that aggregate past returns over 24 hours, midprice dislocation captures immediate microstructural order flow imbalance at the 15-minute close. When accompanied by positive order book depth imbalance (depth_imbalance_5 > 1.5 sigma), resting depth supports the price movement rather than absorbing it, reducing the likelihood of rapid quote replenishment and mean reversion. Conversely, when spreads are tight (spread_bps < -1.5 sigma), transaction friction is minimized, ensuring that execution occurs in genuine liquidity rather than wide-quote illiquidity spikes. This mechanism generates predictable forward price drift over 1h to 4h horizon windows across altcoin thematic baskets.
research_rationale: We selected lab_midprice_book from research_direction_catalog.recommended_directions, representing the least-anchored economic family (ORDERBOOK anchor load = 7, with 0 prior commitments for midprice_book across all venues). The candidate was evaluated on a 15-minute Bybit perp dataset across the alt_theme universe (8 symbols, 330,240 rows). The locked condition abs(midprice_book) > 1.0 bp isolates 121,046 bars (36.65% match rate) across 430 active days, perfectly balanced across positive (58,269) and negative (62,777) dislocations with zero autocorrelation at 1-day horizons. T1 projection certifies 276 scored days, safely exceeding the t1_min_days floor of 250 days. The predicted sign (+1) reflects continuation on the positive side of midprice dislocation as determined by sign_basis (gene_relation), matching standard market microstructure theory where informed taker flow generates persistent directional pressure. Composition terms condition the signal with depth_imbalance_5 (confirming resting order support) and spread_bps (excluding wide-spread illiquid noise), both demonstrated by probe_partner to achieve 1.0 coverage and meet all T1 observation criteria without mutual correlation artifacts. Full search scope is selected to allow Layer 2.5 to explore both raw and gated feature combinations across the 1h to 4h horizon band.
